figures.caption: Figure 1. Same clip, different viewers. Different subjects start the same clip in different brain states (left). EEG-World rolls each viewer’s state forward under the clip and forecasts that viewer’s own response (right); a context-free encoding model predicts the same trajectory for everyone (dashed). Traces are drawn from the forecast band power.
Figure 2. Scale against public EEG datasets recorded during audio-visual stimuli. Hours of EEG while a stimulus is on screen, summed over subjects; bubble area shows hours per subject.

Figure 3. EEG-World. One GRU step per second. In the context, the encoded band power e(xt) updates the latent state; in the rollout a learned blank b replaces it (Eq. (1)). The clip acts through the video pathway g on frozen features, and a shared readout W plus a per-subject head (Ui, ci) give the forecast. Right, a real test viewing chosen for illustration, at the 99.8th percentile of skill.

Figure 4. Scaling on continuous EEG. Forecast correlation on held-out recordings of the 15 core subjects against pooled training EEG; shaded, EEG-World’s lead. Right, all cores and the stateless forecasters at 2,012 h.

Figure 5. Video trials. Held-out clips of the 15 core subjects against the amount of video-paired training EEG. (a) Forecast correlation. (b) Clip-locked correlation (SLv) between the clip-driven part of each forecast and the mean EEG of the other viewers, in percent of the noise ceiling; shaded, below +2 SD of a shuffledclip null.

Figure 6. Unseen subjects. 24 subjects never used in development; frozen models with a per-subject linear head. (a) Gain over the best history + video linear model, in percent of its r, with the subjects ahead. (b) A model retrained without these subjects, against each subject’s own calibration data; dashed, the best linear model fitted on all of it. (c) Correlation lost when the clip is swapped; dots, subjects.

Figure 7. Where, when and what. (a) Gain over the best linear model at each electrode and band, in percent of its r, and the horizon gained. (b) Gain, in percent, against the distance of the starting state from the subject’s mean. (c) In-silico tuning, the forecast change when one input feature is raised, against the tuning of recorded EEG across viewers, for every feature and electrode–band cell; right, maps of two features. Panel (c) uses validation data only.
